documents.title: Artificial Intelligence Language for Syllabi
tiers: AI is encouraged during the course, and appropriate acknowledgement is expected
AI is permitted only for specific assignments or situations, and appropriate acknowledgement is required
AI is not permitted in this course at all
documents.summary: Academic Affairs requires every UT Tyler syllabus to carry common AI language and one of three instructor-chosen categories (encouraged, permitted for specific assignments, not permitted), with sample statements for each. The common language requires acknowledgement of AI use, bars protected or copyrighted data, and sends misuse to the Academic Integrity Policy.
documents.stance_why: The page says "All UT Tyler faculty must identify to what degree students may utilize artificial intelligence (AI) tools" and offers "three basic categories" with sample statements, so the university sets no single stance and hands the choice to instructors, with templates listed in tiers.

documents.summary: Digital Learning guidance names the Microsoft tools UT Tyler licenses, limits what data may go into ChatGPT-type tools, and lists prohibited uses such as grading and decisions about people. It also points to policy, copyright and click-through-contract risks and repeats the duty to state a course AI rule.
documents.stance_why: The page says "All UT Tyler faculty must specify the extent to which students are permitted to use" AI tools, and its own rules concern data, tools and legal use rather than a student-work stance, so the decision on coursework is delegated to instructors.

units.why: "Responsible AI use starts with clear guidelines and a shared commitment to ethical practice" states the purpose and principle of the guidelines, P56.
